core.title: Scope each user/system flow to one coherent journey
core.given: A plan contains a user/system flow and its product capabilities, being authored, edited, or reviewed (including an unchanged existing user/system flow or a product capability change that may alter the user/system flow's journey).
core.when: The planner sets or checks the user/system flow's outcome and which product capabilities it contains.
core.then: The user/system flow must tell ONE coherent journey: if its outcome cannot be stated in one sentence without 'and', split it.
prefer: Size: 3-7 product capabilities is the recommended sweet spot; 2 is the allowed minimum.
At 8-12 product capabilities, review whether the user/system flow holds multiple journeys (split if it does); at 13+, decompose.

Treat these as decomposition signals to investigate (do they mean multiple journeys?): outcome with multiple 'AND's; both setup AND teardown of a lifecycle; mix of exploratory (gesture) and core-mechanic flows; multiple independent feedback loops; participants from 3+ themes.
avoid: User/system flows of 13+ product capabilities (antipattern), e.g. a 16-capability 'complete lifecycle' user/system flow spanning multiple journeys.
Single-capability user/system flows (below the minimum of 2).
core.why: A user/system flow demonstrates one user journey end to end; bundling journeys hides independent outcomes and makes the user/system flow too large to review and accept as one story.
evidence: Reviewer states the user/system flow outcome in one sentence without 'and'.
Product capability count: 3-7 recommended, 2 minimum, 8-12 flagged for review (multiple journeys?), 13+ decompose, 1 below minimum.
Reviewer checks the user/system flow for decomposition signals; each present signal indicates the user/system flow may be multiple journeys.
verification: Scope of the check: it applies to user/system flow specs among the plan artifacts (recognized by plan-artifact kind/location per the profile); an edit confined to a single product capability's internals that changes neither user/system flow membership, outcome, flow kinds, feedback loops nor participant themes is out of scope, as are code changes that do not touch or review user/system flow specs.

Product capability count is mechanically countable and the size bands are part of the obligation: <2 below minimum, 2 minimum allowed, 3-7 recommended, 8-12 flagged for review (multiple journeys?), 13+ decompose.

The one-sentence outcome test (can the user/system flow's outcome be stated in one sentence without 'and'?) is judgment-based: a check may flag the conjunctions, but whether the user/system flow is one journey is judged, not mechanically decidable.

Decomposition signals are investigative, not auto-violations: each present signal only indicates the user/system flow may hold multiple journeys; deciding that it does (and splitting) is a reviewed judgment.

values: user/system flow product capability count changed
product capability flow kind or feedback loop changed

fires: Planner authors a new user/system flow listing its product capabilities and outcome.
Planner adds product capabilities to an existing user/system flow, pushing it to 8 or more.
Planner or reviewer reviews an existing, unchanged user/system flow for scope.
A user/system flow's outcome sentence needs 'and' to describe what it delivers.
A user/system flow has only one product capability.
A product capability edit introduces an exploratory (gesture) flow into a core-mechanic user/system flow, adds an independent feedback loop, or adds participants from another theme.
doesNotFire: Editing a single product capability's internals (e.g. wording of DESIRED OUTCOMES or acceptances) in a way that changes neither user/system flow membership, outcome, flow kind, feedback loops, nor participant themes.
Code changes in implementation layers that do not touch or review user/system flow specs.

neutralityNotes: The core speaks the ATDD plan vocabulary (user/system flow, product capability, journey, DESIRED OUTCOME, flow kinds such as exploratory/gesture vs core-mechanic, feedback loops, participant themes). This is method-level vocabulary assumed shared by every stack realization, not stack machinery; the only stack-dependent input is recognizing user/system flow spec files, taken from the profile via roles.plan_artifact.kinds (kind/location in the plan). The numeric size bands (2 / 3-7 / 8-12 / 13+) are the obligation itself and stay in the core rather than becoming profile data. The named-check/term ids (one_journey_test, decomposition_signal) and the project-specific calibration user/system flow ids (user-system-flow:decision:standard, user-system-flow:match:solo-match-complete) have no stack-neutral equivalent and remain bunOnly; the core's verification names those checks generically. bun.json declares no per-rule severity or disposition, so none is asserted in the core's verification.
